newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurocopter seeks 700 mln Ffr payment from France.
newsitem.headline: Eurocopter seeks 700 mln Ffr payment from France.

text.p: Franco-German helicopter maker Eurocopter is seeking 700 million francs ($126 million) in late payments from the French government for its development of the NH90 military aircraft, its chairman said on Wednesday.

The late payment stems from the government's decision earlier this year to delay until 2010 deliveries of the tactical transport version of the NH90 for the army, Jean-Francois Bigay told journalists. Deliveries had been due to start in 2001/2002.
Eurocopter is 70 percent held by French state-owned Aerospatiale and 30 percent by Daimler-Benz Aerospace.
"The French, who have accepted this programme, which was reconfirmed in the defence budget law, are behind on payments...at the end of 1996, the late payment was 700 million francs," he said.
The non-payment was not a risk to the NH90 programme, he said, adding that he expected the matter to be resolved in the near future.
The French, German, Italian and Dutch governments in the NH90 programme are due to sign a memorandum of understanding (MOU) in the next few weeks confirming orders for the aircraft.

The intergovernmental MOU will allow the prime contractor NH Industries and its industrial partners to negotiate contracts for tooling up and full-scale production which should be signed next year. That should allow NH90 deliveries to start in 2003.
Eurocopter, Agusta SpA of Italy and Fokker Aviation, a unit of Dutch Stork NV are the industrial partners.
The French and German governments are pressing Eurocopter to build the NH90 in a single factory, to cut costs, instead of splitting it between French and German plants.

Bigay said the original MOU setting up the NH90 programme stipulated two assembly lines, one in France, the other in Germany. It was therefore a political decision to decide where the single plant should be located.

Neither country would want to give up its production site, but France would have a weak hand in negotiations as Germany wanted its helicopters as early as 2001 and could claim priority on building the aircraft, a Eurocopter executive said.
France is buying a total 160 NH90s, of which 27 are naval versions and the rest due for the army.
The four nations are buying a total 647 NH90s.
-- Pierre Tran, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.538 French Francs)
